title: Tight Time-Memory Tradeoffs for Additional Randomized Modes
summary: Low-state distinguishing attacks do not rule out good tradeoffs for the candidate modes; proving tight security tradeoffs for them remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether additional randomized CTR, OFB, CBC, and CFB modes admit provably tight time-memory tradeoffs.

scope.domain: Symmetric-encryption modes and tight time-memory security tradeoffs under memory-bounded distinguishing.
parameters: S, memory available to the distinguisher
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether randomized CTR instantiated with a permutation and randomized OFB, CBC, and CFB modes admit proofs of tight time-memory tradeoffs.

citations.label: Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption

progress.summary: The paper presents this as a broader open question after discussing candidate randomized modes. It notes that low-state distinguishing attacks do not rule out good time-memory tradeoffs, leaving tight proofs unresolved.
citation_labels: Joseph Jaeger et al., Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption
